title: QH 207 interpretation delta: 2016 volume -> 2022 BIFAO 'Re-Membering' Osiris

sources.2016: Martin Fitzenreiter, Frank Willer, Johannes Auenmüller, Materialien einer Gusswerkstatt von der Qubbet el-Hawa
sources.2022: Georges Verly, Johannes Auenmüller, Luc Delvaux, Frederik W. Rademakers, 'Re-Membering' Osiris: Late Period Casting Moulds and Osirian Ritual?, BIFAO 122 (2022), 541-571

2016_position.summary: The 2016 interpretive chapter strongly entertains ritual deposition, magical/technical healing and an Osiris dismemberment/reassembly parallel, while treating local sacred-entity linkage as secondary to the broader Osiris myth and funerary transformation framework.

2022_position.summary: The 2022 BIFAO article explicitly advances a more local hypothesis: the anomalous broken/rejoined Osiris bronze-foot practice may have had ritual use in the First Cataract region, with Qubbet el-Hawa's proximity and social connection to Elephantine forming part of the argument.
elephantine_argument: Late Period priests and songstresses buried in QH 207 served the local cults of Khnum and Satet associated with Elephantine.
The paper connects Elephantine with the Osiris leg/feet complex and identifies the left Osiris leg as a locally significant divine relic within dismemberment/revival theology.
The authors relate the Nile inundation in the First Cataract religious landscape to the legs/feet of Osiris and use that context when framing the proposed local ritual use.
2022_position.important_scope_control: The same discussion also notes that theology of the Osiris leg was widespread in the Late Period Egyptian religious landscape rather than unique to Elephantine.

paper_language: possible association with a ritual connected to the revival of Osiris
2022_epistemic_caution.explicit_competing_question: The paper itself asks whether the objects could instead be material remains of experiments on technological feasibility rather than evidence of an Osirian ritual.
2022_epistemic_caution.effect: The 2022 article strengthens and localizes the interpretive hypothesis but does not convert it into demonstrated ritual causation or physical-relic identity.

web_followup_2026_09_16.query_scope: Searches for post-2022 QH 207 / 'Re-Membering Osiris' publications or explicit revisions by Auenmüller, Verly, Fitzenreiter and related authors through 2026.
web_followup_2026_09_16.boundary: This is a search-state statement, not proof that no later revision exists. Author replies, institutional bibliographies, non-indexed proceedings or forthcoming work may supersede it.
notable_hits: The official IFAO 2022 article remains the clearest published local-ritual formulation located.

A later archaeometallurgy volume/project listing continues to describe remarkable mending of Qubbet el-Hawa Osiris figures but, in the indexed abstract found, does not supply a clear later revision of the ritual interpretation.
A 2026 archaeometallurgy article cites the 2022 paper but does not itself provide an identified revision of the QH 207 ritual hypothesis in the search material retrieved.

author_followup_effect.Auenmueller_question_3: NOW_NARROWED: 2022 itself demonstrably advances the local First Cataract/Elephantine hypothesis; the live question is whether Auenmüller still endorses, modifies, weakens or has further evidence for it after 2022.
author_followup_effect.Fitzenreiter_question: NOW_NARROWED: compare his 2016 broader transformation/deposition framing with the 2022 localized hypothesis and ask whether he accepts that localization or regards it as beyond the evidence.
author_followup_effect.Willer_question: UNCHANGED: remains primarily technical/data-oriented (µCT, gilding, custody/documentation).

promotion_rule: Published localization is interpretive evidence, not archaeological proof of a literal relic or a demonstrated causal ritual chain. Promotion above PUBLISHED_HYPOTHESIS requires new primary context, object-level data, independent analytical evidence, or a later source that supplies testable evidence rather than agreement alone.
